descriptors.name: Normalize vector and retain length

descriptors.notes: Arguments are encoded native pointers; valid allocation and lifetime are required. This changes the input vector and does not sanitize NaN values. A zero-length vector keeps xyz unchanged and writes zero to w.

descriptors.name: Create child VM context
descriptors.summary: Creates a child of the current VM context and returns its encoded address as @ADR. Operand 0 is stored as the child mask; when nonzero, existing children satisfying (childMask & operand0) == operand0 are first destroyed. Operand 1 initializes the child PC. Nonzero operand 2 replaces its exit-PC field at +64. Non-NULL decoded operand 3 causes that tagged value to be copied onto the child stack.
descriptors.notes: Uses the current-context global at RVA 0x2A25048 and VM allocator at RVA 0x2A250A0. Child destruction can run exit script code before freeing memory. Allocation failure is not safely returned by the captured creator: it dereferences the resulting child without a NULL guard. No script-PC, pointer-lifetime or concurrency validation is established.

descriptors.summary: Returns @INT indicating whether the resource-request list at RVA 0x2A0D628 is nonempty. The worker changes request states and the completion path invokes stored callbacks before unlinking and freeing requests.

descriptors.notes: No VM return slot. This is mutating resource maintenance, not a general unload-all or lifetime barrier. It can enqueue loads and modify addresses; the complete transitive resource/callback graph is outside this annotation.

descriptors.name: Apply indexed flag action record
descriptors.summary: Sets the grouped flag for operand 0 and interprets its variable-length action record from the table rooted at RVA 0xBF30B0. Actions can change other flags, apply further records recursively, modify stored state and trigger native follow-up functions.
descriptors.notes: This is not a plain bit-setter. Three hard-coded IDs also call RVA 0x210540, and the path includes additional rule propagation. It does not check the ID/table bounds or record length before dereferencing them. The complete meanings of all action opcodes and downstream callbacks remain open.

descriptors.name: Read grouped flag
descriptors.summary: For ID 65535, returns zero. Otherwise reads bit (id & 31) from DWORD index 8*(signed(id)>>10) + ((id & 1023)>>5), based at RVA 0x9AB540. Returns @INT.
descriptors.notes: The signed shift and overlapping grouped indexing are native behavior. IDs other than the explicit 65535 sentinel receive no bounds check; a negative ID is not rejected.

descriptors.name: Random integer
descriptors.summary: Updates the shared DWORD seed at RVA 0x7535C0 by multiplying it by 69069 modulo 2^32. For unsigned n > 0, returns seed / ceil(2^32 / n) as @INT.
descriptors.notes: n = 0 reaches an integer divide fault after updating the seed and the return tag. This describes the native path, not a recommended call.

descriptors.name: Random float scaled
descriptors.summary: Updates the same shared seed, converts the unsigned 32-bit result to float, multiplies by 2^-32 and by operand 0, and returns @FLT.
descriptors.notes: Float rounding can produce a fraction of 1.0. The decompiler shows a misleading signed cast; the instructions zero-extend through EDX before CVTSI2SS from RDX.

descriptors.name: Random float between
descriptors.summary: Updates the shared seed and calculates a + (b - a) * (float(seed) * 2^-32) using scalar float instructions. Returns @FLT.
descriptors.notes: The seed conversion is unsigned. Float rounding can reach an endpoint; no strictly open upper interval is promised.

descriptors.name: Set queued flag
descriptors.summary: Sets the unsigned-indexed bit in the array at RVA 0x9AD8E8 if it is not already set. For IDs 37, 42, 45 and 46, an additional preexisting flag can suppress the operation. A table lookup then decides whether the low byte of the ID is appended to the notification queue.
descriptors.notes: The byte queue cursor at RVA 0x9ADA07 increments with wraparound. The table lookup uses a key encoded as a pointer value and dereferences its result without a NULL check; valid table contents and a matching ID are required. ID 0 becomes a NULL search key; external CRT argument-validation behavior is outside this capture. No guessed game feature name is assigned.

descriptors.name: Integer absolute value
descriptors.summary: Calculates a 32-bit absolute value using CDQ, XOR and SUB, then returns @INT.
descriptors.notes: INT_MIN wraps to the same bit pattern 0x80000000.

descriptors.name: Float absolute value
descriptors.summary: Converts float to double, clears the double sign bit and converts back to float, returning @FLT.
descriptors.notes: NaN payloads and signaling behavior follow those floating-point conversions; this is not a raw float-bit sign mask.

descriptors.summary: Initializes the decoded caller buffer: QWORD +0=0, DWORD +8=112, DWORD +12=1, QWORD +16=1 and DWORD +24=1. No VM return slot.
descriptors.notes: Writes 28 bytes to caller-owned memory without a NULL guard. The later activation path also writes interpolation fields at +28/+32, so activation requires storage beyond these initialized 28 bytes. This call alone does not enable the global effect.

descriptors.name: Enable shared screen effect
descriptors.summary: Sets bit 0 in the decoded parameter buffer and enables the shared rendering state at RVA 0xABC690. It applies mode from +4, alpha byte from +8, position from +12/+16 and float rate from +20 and signed integer duration/count from +24. It also initializes the buffer interpolation pair at +28/+32.
descriptors.notes: The adapter explicitly supplies zero as the interpolation duration; the helper clamps it to one, initializing the pair to (0,1). Coordinate additions use 16-bit wraparound before scaling to current render dimensions. State is shared globally; the caller buffer is also mutated. No NULL or size guard.

descriptors.name: Increase white overlay opacity
descriptors.summary: Divides the float operand by 2, truncates to a signed 32-bit integer and configures the shared overlay at RVA 0xABB3B0. RGB bytes become 255 and the render-mode field becomes 72. State 3 increases alpha toward 128. The update subtracts the native float delta at RVA 0x717484.
descriptors.notes: No finite/range validation. The helper doubles the converted value modulo 2^32 and then converts that zero-extended DWORD to float; negative inputs can therefore become large positive durations, and wrapped zero can reach a reciprocal divide by zero. An originally zero converted value instead selects duration 2 and slope 1. Units are native update units, not proven wall seconds. State 4 can invoke another native continuation after reaching alpha 128; its full effect remains open.

descriptors.name: Turn direction toward vector

For finite nonnegative operand2 * tickFactor, the rotation angle is min(angle, operand2 * tickFactor). It sets the local direction w to zero before the matrix transform, then copies the result into operand 0.
descriptors.notes: The adapter replaces NaN components of the referenced input vector(s) with zero in place. The native float operand 2 is passed in XMM3; tickFactor is global 0x717480. Zero and antiparallel vectors have no special axis fallback, so intermediate results need not remain unit length. Negative and nonfinite inputs follow the raw COMISS/MAXSS branches. Encoded pointers require valid native objects and live storage; the adapter does not validate their type or lifetime.

descriptors.notes: The adapter neither checks for NULL nor identifies the allocator that originally produced the pointer. The active allocator can change during region transitions, so allocation provenance and lifetime remain required.

Snapshots counter RVA 0xABB850 and sets state 1; the next unpaused timer task changes it to state 2 before updating the count.
descriptors.notes: Counter progress is driven by the installed timing callback and can be paused through RVA 0xABB854. The factor 60 establishes the native conversion, not exact elapsed wall seconds. Countdown clamps at zero; count-up clamps at 215999 and otherwise stops on a positive configured limit. Limit completion dispatches native call 3AABE0(74,0). Input multiplication can wrap; no argument bounds are checked.
